title: Uncovering and Categorizing Social Biases in Text-to-SQL
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypical correlations and discriminative comparisons involving religious groups in Text-to-SQL models. The benchmark measures if models generate biased SQL queries linking judgmental modifiers (e.g., 'worse', 'terrible') in natural language questions to religious identities in the database schema, even when no such link is prompted.
findings: Text-to-SQL models tend to generate biased SQL queries that create stereotypical correlations between judgmental terms (e.g., 'freakish', 'dangerous') and religious groups (e.g., 'Muslim'). These models incorrectly infer religious attributes from unrelated columns to satisfy biased queries, even when the original question and database schema have no explicit connection between the judgment and the religion.
